floater.name: wolf_vr_stream
floater.title: VR in Your Headset
floater.floater.string: Off. Nothing is listening on your network.
On. In your headset's browser, type the address below.
Your headset is connected. Press Enter VR in the headset. Right controller: point, trigger = click, grip = right-click, stick = scroll and turn. Left stick walks.

Your headset is connected. Press Enter VR in the headset. Look around; left stick walks, right stick turns and flies. Point with the right controller: the trigger touches or clicks what it points at, B opens its menu (for example Sit Here). The Menu tab in front of you (or the left menu button) opens the action bar. Your HUDs and windows show in front of you; HUDs on the bar hides them. Left stick click switches to the big screen.
floater.text: See WolfViewer in your VR headset's own web browser (Meta Quest Browser), over your home network. Nothing to install on the headset.

check_box.name: enable
check_box.label: Stream to my headset
check_box.tool_tip: Starts a small web server on this PC's home-network address only. Turn it off and it stops at once.

combo_box.name: mode
combo_box.tool_tip: Where the headset starts (you can switch in the headset any time: left stick click). What the headset shows. VR Big Screen Mode: the whole WolfViewer window on a large screen in front of you, with the controllers as the mouse. VR 3D Mode: you are in the world, and it follows your head. You can also switch in the headset (left stick click).

radio_group.name: headset
radio_group.tool_tip: Automatic works it out from the headset's browser and lowers the picture quality by itself if your headset or network cannot keep up.

floater.text: A Meta Quest or PICO names itself and uses its own settings. To choose differently, choose on the headset page.

radio_group.name: sound_out
radio_group.tool_tip: Headset: everything you would hear on this PC - the world, voice chat, sounds of the viewer - plays in the headset, and this PC's speakers are quiet while it does.

check_box.name: headset_mic
check_box.label: Use the headset microphone for voice
check_box.tool_tip: Off: your PC's microphone is used for voice chat. On: the headset's own microphone is used while the headset plays the sound (the headset browser asks you once if it may use it).

check_box.name: hide_avatar
check_box.label: Hide my avatar in VR 3D Mode (see from my own eyes)
check_box.tool_tip: Off: you see your avatar from just behind and above, as on your screen. On: you see the world from your avatar's eyes and your avatar is not shown in the headset. Hide Me on the VR bar does the same.

text_editor.name: address
text_editor.tool_tip: Type this into the headset browser's address bar. No code is needed.

floater.text: No code needed. Or open wolf-grid.com/vr in the headset and type it there.

The first time only: the headset browser says the connection is not private. Choose Advanced, then Proceed (this PC made its own certificate; the picture never leaves your home network). Then press Enter VR. Tip: bookmark the page in the headset.
With a USB cable and developer mode instead: run "adb reverse tcp:[PORT] tcp:[PORT]" on this PC, then open:

text_editor.name: usb_url
text_editor.tool_tip: For a headset plugged in by USB, after adb reverse

button.name: codec_download
button.label: Download
button.tool_tip: Downloads the free OpenH264 video codec from Cisco (about 1 MB), for a sharp, smooth picture in the headset.
